draft.title: Context of composition
card: Context of composition is the set of circumstances in which a text was written. It can be historical, social or personal.
Historical
the events and period of the time, such as a war or an economic depression.
Social
the values and ways of living in the writer's community, such as ideas about class or gender.
Personal
the writer's own life and experiences, such as where they grew up or what they lived through. Knowing the context helps explain a text's concerns, but a text is more than a record of its time.
draft.remember: Context helps explain why a text was written as it was, but it does not replace reading the text itself.

a.q: A novel was written just after a long war and shows families struggling to rebuild. How does knowing this context help a reader?
opts: It helps explain why the novel deals with loss and rebuilding
It proves the novel is only a record of that war
It shows the novel has no ideas beyond the war
It tells the reader what the novel's ending must be
a.why: Knowing the time of writing helps explain the text's concerns, such as loss and rebuilding. It does not prove the novel is only a record of the war, because a text is more than a record of its time.
a.clue: Context helps explain concerns. Does it limit the text to them?

b.q: Priya writes that a poet's poems about leaving home are explained by the poet's own migration from another country. Which kind of context is Priya using?
opts: Personal context
Historical context
Social context
Context of reception
b.why: The poet's own migration is part of the writer's life, so it is personal context. It is not social context, which is about the values and ways of living of a whole community. Reception is about later readers, not the writer's circumstances.
b.clue: Whose life is the explanation drawn from?
